title: Claude Code works out Wordle's repeated-letter rules and builds a working clone
summary: A developer used REA with Claude Code to study how Wordle scores guesses, including repeated letters, and then build their own version based on that logic rather than copying the interface.
agent_role: The agent studied how Wordle behaves, including how it handles repeated letters, and implemented a matching version. The human picked the target and directed the work.
outcome: Author shows a working Wordle clone in a video demo.
what_they_did: The poster used a tool called REA together with Claude Code to reverse-engineer Wordle. They had the agent work out the game's logic, including how repeated letters are marked, and then build a version of their own.
how_it_went: The author shares a video of the result and says the agent studied the logic behind the game instead of just copying the UI.
prompt: Investigate how [game name] works by studying its observable behavior. Write down its rules precisely, including edge cases such as [tricky case, e.g. repeated letters in a guess]. Show me the rule list and a set of test cases first and wait for my approval. Then build a web version in [framework] that passes those tests.

curation.rationale: A genuine agent task, with a video demo: the agent worked out Wordle's rules, including repeated letters, and built a clone. The post is brief and gives few details about REA or the steps.
